title: A directional zero–one law for finite-range-dependent random environments
main_claim: For a uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbour RWRE on Z^d (d>=3) whose law is stationary and has finite-range dependence of transition rows (also for infinite index sets), P_0(X_n·l -> +infinity) is 0 or 1 for every fixed nonzero real direction l.
coverage: I read every manuscript file under build/manuscript: main, history, cuts, radius, bridges, entropy, posteriors and conclusion. I checked these steps line by line. (1) Lemma 2.1 (separated weights) and the script-gap separation: active rows lie below r, continuation rows at r+M or higher, and M>dR gives l-infinity distance >R. (2) Prop 2.2: the regeneration law via enumeration of finite prefixes, uniqueness of parsing, and the test argument for existence of a cut. (3) Sign union, and finite mean width via record counting and the renewal-density argument. (4) Prop 3.2 radius moment: the constants inequalities, the maximal lemma, the second-moment selection of a large excursion, the tilted-Y gap computation (a(m0 b-1-bC0+(bc-1)k)-m0 > R(1+dba)), the tail height gap using C1 c > C+4, and the final-supremum windows contradiction. (5) Opposite rays via the tail zero-one law, and the coordinate reduction. (6) Exact-cut bridges u-bar_H = xi u_{H-M} and the width-tail lemma: the renewal difference identity, the exceptional index k=n+1 and the constant (1+xi)/xi. (7) Common blocks renewal: c_n >= xi^2 p+ p-, finite mean, and the Wald-type radius bound. (8) Entropy comparison: the chunk density, D_0 <= C, the buffer information identity, the chain of entropy inequalities giving 2D_0 + H(T,Z+X_B) - H(I0,d0), and the bound C + h'_{14n} - h'_n. (9) Reference contact bound: first-proximity truncation, the transfer to a shared environment, the height window inequalities, the quenched exit dichotomy with kappa^{dR}, and the bound by u_n - u_N <= C N F(n). (10) The dyadic summation giving O(J/log J). (11) The posterior-max lemma: the Ville/entropy bound on the remaining increase, the threshold geometric tail and the event-weighted bound. (12) Prop 6.2: the exact prefix-sum identity, the stopped-path law equality that justifies transferring the posterior martingale, the bin decomposition and the final Delta log^2 bound. (13) The contact lower bound: the parameters k,r, Delta <= C 2^{-G} a_l, the phi monotonicity and slow-tail bound, the o(J) count, unconditioning by xi p+, and the depth-to-block-index conversion. Every algebraic step I checked by hand holds; I found no sign, constant or quantifier error. I did not open the companion iid paper. This paper states that it proves the needed estimates itself, and I confirmed it does not rely on any unproved companion lemma.
